recommendations.summary: Lock Nash (LW, 20, $1.20M expiring) on a 5-6 year deal
recommendations.rationale: 20 years old, first-round talent, core lock. 5-6 years at $1.20M is the cheapest possible lock for a future top-six winger.

recommendations.summary: Lock Eminger (D, 21, $1.20M expiring) on a 5-6 year deal
recommendations.rationale: GM vetoed trading Eminger for Chara on 2005-01-19, explicitly saying POTE 99 at 21 is worth more than Chara at 27. He is the future top-pair D and needs a long deal.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour (G, 39, $6.50M expiring) a reduced deal at renewal; plan for his departure if he declines
recommendations.rationale: GM's own standing order from Jan 15: 'I would offer him a reduced contract at renewal but he probably won't accept.' At $6.50M and 39, this is the single largest payroll item and the most likely departure.

recommendations.summary: No deadline blueliner needed; Eminger (21, POTE 99), Colaiacovo (22), and Stahle (20, POTE 96) cover next season's blue line
recommendations.rationale: The Coach flags Stahle at 2 GP in 53 games and needs ice time, but that is a lineup decision. The roster already has three young D with real potential; buying another at the deadline blocks their development and spends a pick we are trying to recover.

recommendations.proposed: Komisarek (MTL, D, 23, 80 ovr, 83 TOUG, 64 pts, POTE 91, $1.10M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Package Upshall plus 4th-rounder to Montreal for Komisarek when negotiations open late February
recommendations.rationale: MTL at 15-30-4 with 14 expiring deals will not re-sign a defenceman they can only rent; they collect youth. Upshall's POTE 99 is expendable because Spezza (POTE 99) and Chlup (POTE 95) already sit ahead of him. Commission closes the toughness gap from the blueline for five years.

recommendations.current: Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99, D, $1.10M) + Tucker (29, 92 CHKG, $1.30M, 3 GP)
recommendations.summary: Offer Colaiacovo plus Tucker to Ottawa for Havlat; OTT's $26M profit absorbs both salaries
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 18-25-6 with 11 expiring deals are comfortable sellers. Colaiacovo at POTE 99 gives them a long-term defenceman; Tucker at 92 CHKG fills their bottom-six immediately. Havlat's 70 points at 23 fills the secondary-scoring hole behind Gaborik without touching the core.

recommendations.current: Chistov (21, POTE 95, 16 pts, $1.10M) + Safronov (23, POTE 91, D, $0.90M)
recommendations.summary: Send Chistov plus Safronov to Calgary for Conroy as a pure faceoff rental through the playoffs
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 16-29-6 with 42 points are the worst team and motivated to shed salary. They get two players with three total team-years of control for an expiring 31-year-old. Conroy's 94 FACE is the only way to win draws against a first line that dumps in; Chistov's 16 points in 39 games is not core production at 21 when Alexeev (30 pts, POTE 94) already sits ahead.

recommendations.proposed: Luongo as starter through playoffs, Belfour as backup and insurance
recommendations.summary: Carry both Luongo (91, $1.60M, 2yr) and Belfour (92 base, $6.50M, expiring) through the playoffs; decide Belfour's renewal in July.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 18-3-0 in 21 starts; Luongo is morale 99 at 91 base. Toronto at 38-9-3 can afford the platoon and the $6.50M is expiring. No need to move either before July.

recommendations.summary: Put Spezza back in the lineup at third-line centre minimum 10 MPG; his morale at 86 is the lowest on the roster and he has POTE 99 at 21 with 7.5 MPG and a scratch.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza's 7.5 MPG and scratch status have held his rate at 0.41 pts/g while his morale drops. Every other scratched youngster has a reason (Koltsov is a chip, Upshall isn't producing, Smirnov has POTE 70). Spezza does not.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle and give him real minutes; 2 GP in 53 games at POTE 96 and age 20 is not development, it's neglect.
recommendations.rationale: Stahle played 17 MPG in his 2 appearances, showing the staff trusts him when he suits up. He needs consistent dressings before the deadline to build anything.

recommendations.summary: No changes needed for Gaborik, Nash, Chlup, Klesla, Eminger, Colaiacovo, or Chistov — they are all getting appropriate minutes and production for their age and role.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik leads the team in points (73 in 53). Nash at 20 is producing 0.80 pts/g on the third line. Chlup at 18 plays second-line minutes. The young D pair (Klesla, Eminger) and Colaiacovo are all in the lineup.

recommendations.summary: Upshall and Smirnov stay scratched — Upshall's 0.38 pts/g doesn't justify a promotion despite POTE 99, and Smirnov's POTE 70 is the lowest on the list.
recommendations.rationale: Upshall has had 45 games to show his POTE 99 and has 17 points on 10.7 MPG. Smirnov has zero games but the lowest scouting number among the young group. Neither warrants a lineup spot over producing players.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 12+ MPG starting now; six consecutive windows at 5-9 MPG means he is losing a year.
recommendations.rationale: Minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 5.3 MPG, rate fell from 0.43 to 0.38 in 37 games. At 21 with POTE 99, 5.3 MPG is not development.

recommendations.summary: Dress Smirnov before the deadline; 20 years old and zero games in the entire season.
recommendations.rationale: Zero GP across both windows. Same situation Stahle was in before he finally got 2 games. At 20 he is wasting away.

recommendations.summary: Chlup stays where he is; 0.72 pts/g at 18 on 15.7 MPG is the right trajectory and don't disrupt it.
recommendations.rationale: Rate climbing from 0.62, minutes climbing from 11.0, still 18. Let him develop naturally.

recommendations.summary: Chistov earns his spot on the first line: 0.48 pts/g on 15.3 MPG, both up sharply.
recommendations.rationale: Rate doubled from 0.29 to 0.48 in 39 games while minutes rose from 9.5 to 15.3. He belongs there.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven changes tonight; only Spezza is below 90 (at 86) and that is the GM's deliberate rotation.
recommendations.rationale: Every other player reads 92+ with stable or rising trends. No minutes-related morale issue exists that a line change would fix.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour if his fatigue icon is clear; Luongo at 91 is the fallback.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour's ENDU 94 and REBC 88 suit a low-event game where TB generates only 1.80 goals per game. If the tired icon shows, switch to Luongo whose AGIL 93 and SREC 89 match Khabibulin's 92 OVR.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for Tampa Bay.
recommendations.rationale: Auto-pairing gives us favorable matchups on lines 2-4 (their L3 centres at 69 OVR) and our L1 has Gaborik at 94 against their top line. TB's PP is 10.9% so no PK adjustment needed. Current assignment already has all key players in.

recommendations.summary: Trade Eminger at the deadline — he hit the 0.45 pts/g threshold I set on January 26th and his $1.2M deal expires in June.
recommendations.rationale: 19 points in 42 games (0.45 pts/g), 73 OVR at 21, expiring contract. I set this exact threshold on Jan 26th. He's there now.

recommendations.summary: Salo at $2.6M x 2 with 8 points in 22 games and not dressed is dead money. Find a buyer before June.
recommendations.rationale: 0.36 pts/g, 30 years old, 79 OVR, two years remaining on a $2.6M contract. He is not in the lineup and the production does not justify the money.

recommendations.summary: Stahle has played 2 games in 53. He needs to be dressed and used regularly or we lose a year on a POTE-96 defenceman at 20.
recommendations.rationale: 2 GP, 34 total minutes, 0 points. Age 20, 67 OVR, POTE 96. The Jan 25 note said 'at least one dressing before the deadline' — he has two now, that's not enough.

recommendations.summary: Colaiacovo is a secondary trade candidate: 69 OVR, 0.43 pts/g, expiring $1.1M. Bundle with Eminger or let walk.
recommendations.rationale: 12 points in 28 games at age 22 with 69 OVR. The ceiling is third-pair. Expiring deal means value in a trade now or nothing in July.

recommendations.summary: Avery closes the toughness and faceoff gaps simultaneously at $400K and age 25, the cheapest single move that addresses both structural holes.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto have zero players at 80+ toughness and one at 80+ faceoffs (Sundin, 33). Avery at 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG fills both. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: Dress Tucker nightly; his 83 CHKG adds a seventh 80+ checker at no cost.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker is on the roster at 83 displayed checking and 29 years old but carries no unit assignment. He is the only internal fix to the checking depth problem.

recommendations.summary: Scoring, speed, stamina, clutch and playmaking are all covered with 9-22 players at 80+; do not spend trade assets on these roles.
recommendations.rationale: The roster has 12 scorers, 22 speed players and 12 stamina players above 80. The gaps are toughness (0 at 80+) and faceoffs (1 at 80+). Spend only on those.

recommendations.summary: There is no successor to Sundin at faceoffs; the next-best centre draws at 75. This gap widens every season he plays.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin at 33 is already declining (0.93 pts/g, down from higher). Chlup at 75 and Richards at 70 cannot replace his 90. By 2006-07 Toronto would have no 80+ faceoff man.

recommendations.summary: The two best checkers on the blue line are 38 and 36; the next-best is McCabe at 86 and declining. The defensive core needs youth within two seasons.
recommendations.rationale: Roberts 86 CHKG at 38 and Svehla 83 at 36 are both past their peak. Fischer at 82 is declining per the coach (0.63 to 0.41). Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 is the internal answer but needs time.

recommendations.summary: Belfour is covered today but is 39 on $6.50M with one year left. The backup depth is a 76-average Tellqvist and an 8-game Ouellet. Luongo remains the target but the R1 Toronto need is blocked.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is playing 0.911 SV and will not be here next year at this salary. Tellqvist averages 76 across his goalie grades. Ouellet at 86 GSH shows promise in 8 games. The Luongo package requires a first-rounder Toronto do not own.

recommendations.summary: Move all three expiring 30+ veterans at the March deadline for draft picks using the over-80 expiring mechanic; recovers draft capital from zero.
recommendations.rationale: Combined $12.80M in expiring salary, all above 80 overall, none planned for re-signing. Belfour is the standing-order trade target. Svehla is already scratched. Roberts has no future. Each qualifies independently for the pick-recovery mechanic.

recommendations.summary: Lock the five expiring core players on long deals in July; accept the salary bump from $6.40M combined to roughly $11-13M and remove them from the 2005 cluster permanently.
recommendations.rationale: All five expire the same summer with POTE 88-99. The manual's warning about simultaneous renewals is exactly this. Locking at once is the only fix since mid-contract renegotiation is impossible. At current production (Gaborik 72 pts, Richards 53, Nash 31 at age 20) their renewal prices will only rise.

recommendations.proposed: acquire young asset or pick in return
recommendations.summary: Plan to move Mogilny (35, $5.50M, 0.87 pts/g, 2 years left) at the next deadline or in July 2006 while he retains trade value.
recommendations.rationale: His production halved from 1.62 to 0.87 pts/g. At $5.50M over two remaining years that is $11.00M for a third-line winger. By the time his deal expires he is 37 and untradeable.

recommendations.summary: Set a diary entry for July 2007: Chlup becomes a free agent at 20 with POTE 95 and his $2.34M rookie salary gone. Lock immediately.
recommendations.rationale: At 18 with 28 points in 41 games, his next contract will be set by a full top-nine season. The 2-year window is his last cheap year after this one.

recommendations.summary: Execute the December 22 three-deal package: Mogilny+R2 for Jackman, R3 for Sillinger, Safronov+R4 for Sutton.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny has halved to 0.87 pts/g at 35 on multiple years of contract. The package dumps his salary, adds toughness (Jackman), faceoffs (Sillinger 96 FACE), and depth (Sutton) for zero first-round capital. It has been pending since December and remains the best value on the board.

recommendations.proposed: Craig Conroy (CGY, C, 31, 63 pts, 94 FACE, $2.00M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Conroy as a deadline rental for Chistov plus a fourth-rounder.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 40 points is a confirmed seller with $2.00M expiring. Conroy's 94 FACE and 63 points fill the centre depth gap for the playoff run. Chistov at 21/$1.10M is the most movable young asset not flagged for development by the Coach.

recommendations.current: Svehla (D, 36, $3.60M, over-80, expiring) + Roberts (LW, 38, $2.70M, over-80, expiring)
recommendations.proposed: Draft pick via over-80 expiring mechanic
recommendations.summary: Trade Svehla and/or Roberts to a contender before March 19 to recover a mid-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: Both are above 80, expiring, and will not be re-signed. The mechanic trades them for a pick. This recovers draft capital that Toronto currently lacks (best owned pick is a fourth-rounder). Combined $6.30M freed is budget for a summer goalie.

recommendations.current: Gaborik (RW, 22, 91 base, 67 pts/45 GP, $1.10M, 1 year left)
recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to 6 years immediately at season end; this is the first call of the summer.
recommendations.rationale: At 91 base with POTE 90 on $1.10M he is the cheapest top-line winger in the league. A 5-6 year deal is standard for a star. Letting him test the market at 22 risks losing a generational asset. The 17-player expiry cluster makes staggering essential; he is the top of that list.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards to 5 years in the same window as Gaborik.
recommendations.rationale: At 24 and $1.00M he is the long-term centre behind Sundin. Five years keeps him off the market at age 29. Signing him the same summer as Gaborik staggers from the 2006 cluster.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle to 5 years. Top-pair defenceman, 26, already producing.
recommendations.rationale: He is the established top-pair blueliner and the Coach needs him there. Five years at 26 locks him through his prime. The $1.90M becomes a bargain by year three.

recommendations.current: Nash (LW, 20, $1.20M, expiring) and Eminger (D, 21, $1.20M, POTE 99, expiring)
recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash and Eminger to 5 years each. Both are 20-21 on $1.20M rookie deals.
recommendations.rationale: Eminger's POTE 99 is the GM's explicit timeline bet. Nash at 20 with first-round talent needs a home. Signing both now at $1.20M is the cheapest option available. Five years keeps them through age 25-26.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign the depth group on 2-year deals to stagger the renewal cluster away from the 5-year core.
recommendations.rationale: The manual warns against contract clustering. These five are depth, not stars, and two years keeps them cheap and off the market in 2007 when the core renewals come due.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Luongo, Kovalchuk, or any target requiring a first-round pick until the Svehla/Roberts over-80 mechanic recovers one.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto owns no pick better than a fourth-rounder. Florida demands R1 for Luongo (confirmed 2005-01-25). ATL demands R1 for Kovalchuk. The over-80 expiring mechanic on Svehla or Roberts is the only realistic path to recovering a mid-round pick by March. If it works, revisit in February.

recommendations.summary: Primary deadline target: Avery closes toughness and faceoffs simultaneously at $400K with two years left.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are motivated sellers. Avery at 25 carries 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG. Package: Chistov plus 4th, both expendable.

recommendations.summary: Backup target if LA refuse Avery: Bell at 24 closes all three gaps on a re-signable deal.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 42 points with 10 expiring are sellers. Bell at 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, $900K, 2 years. Package: Colaiacovo plus Safronov (no R2 available).

recommendations.summary: Highest-production available player: Marleau at 79 pts in 52 games, age 25, fills the Mogilny succession gap.
recommendations.rationale: SJ at 49 points with 14 expiring cannot re-sign him. $1.60M expiring. TOUG 50 and FACE 67 mean he does not solve the structural gaps, only scoring depth.

recommendations.summary: Cheaper SJ option: Sturm at 69 pts in 52 games, 90 SPEE, $1.00M with one year left, replaces Mogilny's production decline.
recommendations.rationale: Same SJ seller as Marleau. At 26 with POTE 74 his ceiling is lower but his 1.33 pts/g current rate is exactly what Mogilny (0.87) used to be. Half the salary.

recommendations.summary: Pure-rental faceoff fix for the playoff run if Avery is blocked: Conroy at 94 FACE, 63 pts, expiring.
recommendations.rationale: CGY at 42 points with 10 expiring will deal. Costs Chistov plus a 4th. Solves nothing beyond this spring; use only if neither Avery nor Bell closes.

recommendations.summary: Five-year top-six solution: both LA wings at 22 with POTE 98 and 96 on expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 48 points with 13 expiring are sellers. Combined $2.20M for two 1.17+ pts/g wingers with POTE 96+. Competes with Avery for the Chistov asset; choose one path.

recommendations.summary: Replaces McCabe's declining 0.52 pts/g with a 22-year-old producing at 1.20 pts/g and POTE 91.
recommendations.rationale: MTL at 42 points with 14 expiring are in full rebuild. Komisarek at $1.10M expiring is a first-pair D in waiting. Package likely requires a young player plus the 4th.

recommendations.summary: Dead at confirmed price: FLA only accept Aebischer plus R1, which Toronto do not own. Monitor for alternative goalie targets.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo at 91 base, POTE 96, age 25, $1.60M, 2 years fits the GM mandate exactly. But FLA's confirmed price includes a first-rounder we do not possess. No path unless price shifts.

recommendations.summary: Dump Svehla ($2.80M) and Roberts ($3.50M) as over-80 expiring assets for draft picks before the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Both 36+ and expiring, both over 80 overall, qualifying for the expiring-asset mechanic. Recovers draft capital from players with no future. Combined $6.30M freed.

recommendations.summary: Open with LA in late February: Chistov plus our 4th for Avery. Closes toughness and faceoffs at a net $700K saving.
recommendations.rationale: Avery at 25 with 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG on $400K/2yr is the cheapest player closing both structural gaps. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring need young speed bodies for a rebuild; Chistov is 21, POTE 95, SPEE 89. Acceptance is uncertain because LA's AI valuation is unknown.

recommendations.summary: If LA refuse Avery, open with CHI: Colaiacovo plus Safronov for Bell. Closes all three gaps on a re-signable deal.
recommendations.rationale: Bell at 24 with 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 80 base on $900K/2yr is the only player closing toughness, checking and faceoffs on a multi-year deal. CHI at 42 points with $26M profit value young D; Colaiacovo POTE 99 at 22 is a top-pair piece. Eminger (POTE 99, 21) and Klesla (POTE 97, 22) fill the D slots behind him. Acceptance uncertain because CHI's profit means they can hold out for more.

recommendations.summary: Long-term swing at LA: two 22-year-olds with POTE 98 and 96 replacing the Mogilny/Sundin wing scoring by 2007. Competes with proposals one and two for the same assets.
recommendations.rationale: Cammalleri 1.17 pts/g and Frolov 1.18 pts/g at 22 on $1.10M expiring from a club that cannot re-sign them. LA get a POTE 99 defenceman, a POTE 95 winger, and a pick. The catch: both expire July 2005, adding $2-3M each to renewal demands on top of the $2.20M cluster already due. Only pursue if proposals one and two are blocked by the same window.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle for Florida and give him real minutes; 2 games in 52 for a 20-year-old POTE-96 defenceman is the biggest waste on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Same flag as January 25th and nothing has changed. POTE 96, age 20, 2 GP. The blue line needs a young body and he is already assigned to the second pair in the lines menu.

recommendations.summary: Raise Alexeev from 8.6 to 12+ MPG; 30 points on fourth-line minutes is the most efficient young production on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 52 games on 8.6 MPG yields 0.58 pts/g. He is producing like a top-nine forward on bottom-six ice. Florida is a weak opponent and a good night to test him at more minutes.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza a line and 12+ minutes; POTE 99 at 21 on 7.5 MPG and scratched is the same flag from January 5th and he is going backwards in usage.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza has 15 points in 37 games at 7.5 MPG. POTE 99 means the club rates his ceiling very high. At 21 he needs a consistent role or the development window narrows. The GM has been rotating him in and then sitting him; neither state is a real chance.

recommendations.summary: Keep Upshall scratched; his January hot stretch has faded to 0.38 pts/g on 10.7 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Fourth-line production on fourth-line minutes. The promotion signal from January 8th (0.69 rate) did not hold. No reason to reinstate him over Nash or Chistov.

recommendations.summary: Spezza at 5.3 MPG and 0.38 pts/g is a wasted development year; he needs 12+ minutes or the window closes.
recommendations.rationale: His minutes fell from 9.1 to 5.3 and his rate fell from 0.43 to 0.38 simultaneously. At 21 he cannot develop on bench minutes. This is the fifth time I have raised it.

recommendations.summary: McCabe's recent window (0.50 pts/g from 1.42) confirms the collapse; plan a summer move or demotion before his value drops further.
recommendations.rationale: A 29-year-old dropping from 1.42 to 0.50 with no ice-time excuse is not a blip. Eminger at 0.61 and rising deserves the top-pair role now.

recommendations.summary: Eminger's recent window at 0.61 pts/g on 17.9 MPG confirms he is a first-pair defenceman for next season; promote his role now.
recommendations.rationale: 0.35 in first 23 games to 0.61 in last 18 is a genuine improvement. At 21 on an expiring deal, he needs to see first-pair minutes now to prove the next contract.

recommendations.summary: Sundin and Mogilny declining is expected at their ages; Gaborik at 1.36 and Abid at 1.30 are still productive enough to keep the current structure.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin dropped to 0.89 but is still getting 19.9 MPG and leading the team. No replacement exists on this roster for any of them. Ride them out.

recommendations.summary: No morale-driven line changes needed; the room is at 86 minimum and the -4 on Mogilny and Sundin is results-driven, not minutes-driven.
recommendations.rationale: Mogilny (17.9 MPG, above his band) and Sundin (18.5 MPG, near his band) both dropped 4 from a points-streak dip. Spezza at 86 is the known cost of the GM's development rotation and is not yet in crisis territory.

recommendations.summary: Unit composition is correct across all eight units for Florida.
recommendations.rationale: L1 carries the best checking mean (79) and elite scoring (87). L2 is the offensive line by design. L3 has the best checking mean at 72 via Klesla's 92. The pair order keeps McCabe/Fischer (both 82 checking) on pair 1 where the auto-pairing puts them against the opponent's best line.

recommendations.summary: We need a centre who wins faceoffs above 70%. Sundin (89) and Chlup (76) are the only two on the roster, leaving L3 at 56 mean and L4 at 51.
recommendations.rationale: Every non-first-line centre on the roster wins fewer than 6 in 10 draws. This is a roster-level gap that no line rearrangement fixes; it needs a transaction deadline target.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo in Florida; Belfour was tired on January 19th and this opponent scores 1.6 per night.
recommendations.rationale: FLA generates 1.6 GF/g and an 11.9% power play. Luongo at 93 OVR is more than enough, and Belfour at 39 needs rest with February loading up.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle on the third pair for this game; Florida's third line is 71/77/72 OVR.
recommendations.rationale: Stahle has 96 POTE at 20 and zero games played. Their L3 is Messier/Nedorost/Kolnik at 71-77-72. Auto-pairing gives our D3 that line. The safest possible debut.

recommendations.summary: Keep all forward lines as they are; the talent gap makes matchup adjustments pointless.
recommendations.rationale: Our top six averages 87 OVR against their top six at 78. Nieuwendyk's FACE 94 on their centre is the only individual edge they hold, and Sundin at 89 with 93 HERO handles it.

recommendations.summary: No defence changes for Florida. McCabe and Fischer are monitored but no line move is warranted yet.
recommendations.rationale: McCabe at 0.92 season rate still earns the top pair. Eminger at 0.46 is near the 0.45 trade threshold but hasn't crossed it. Stahle finally playing (2 GP, 17 MPG) is progress. Nothing has moved enough to change the pairings.

recommendations.summary: Lock the five stars whose contracts expire this July onto 5-6 year deals before any trade talks open; without these signatures the 2006 roster has no core.
recommendations.rationale: Fifteen contracts worth $25.30M hit the same summer. Gaborik (72 pts, 91 base, POTE 90, 22) is the most urgent; Nash (30 pts, POTE 95, 20) and Eminger (POTE 99, 21) are the cheapest long-term value. Richards at 51 pts and $1.00M is the least glamorous lock but still a first-line centre at 24.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla and Roberts to contender clubs via the over-80 expiring mechanic to recover first and second-round picks, which are the only currency the club lacks.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla ($3.60M, 36, 23 pts/34 GP, 1yr) and Roberts ($2.70M, 38, 59 pts/51 GP, 1yr) are both above 80 overall and expiring. A contender needing depth D or a veteran wing at the deadline pays picks for them. Toronto has no pick better than a 4th, which blocks the Luongo package requiring an R1.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup from his current two years onto a 5-6 year deal before his rookie-window price of $2.34M erases after a full top-nine season.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup is 18 with POTE 95 on $2.34M with 2 years left. If he produces 50+ points next year at 19, his renewal price in 2006 will be dramatically higher. Locking him now at a modest escalation preserves the cheapest star on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Move Svehla (D, 36, $3.60M expiring) before the March 19 deadline for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: He is 36, expensive, and gone in July regardless. The over-80 mechanic turns him into a pick, which we currently lack. Open the conversation in late February.

recommendations.summary: Move Roberts (LW, 38, $2.70M expiring) before the March 19 deadline for a draft pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic.
recommendations.rationale: Same logic as Svehla: 38, $2.70M, expiring, above 80. Trade for a pick rather than losing him for nothing in July. Combined with Svehla this recovers $6.30M and two picks.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour (G, 39, $6.50M) a reduced contract at renewal; if he refuses, trade him at the deadline for a pick.
recommendations.rationale: GM standing order says Belfour stays. His $6.50M is the largest contract on the roster. A reduced deal keeps him; refusal makes him a third over-80 expiring chip tradeable for a pick.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik (RW, 22, 91 base, POTE 90, 67 pts/45 GP, $1.10M) on five to six years before the July market opens.
recommendations.rationale: He is the best player on the roster, 22 years old, and the current deal expires after this season. A five or six year lock prevents a bidding war and keeps him cheap.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Eminger (D, 21, POTE 99, $1.20M) on five to six years.
recommendations.rationale: The GM killed the Chara deal specifically to keep Eminger. At 21 with POTE 99 he is the franchise blueliner. Lock him long.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards (C, 24, $1.00M) on five to six years.
recommendations.rationale: Core centre, 24, cheap at $1.00M. The December note flagged him as a staggered lock. Five to six years prevents the same-summer cluster problem.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle (D, 26, $1.90M) on four to five years.
recommendations.rationale: He is 26, on an expiring deal, and a top-four blueliner. Four to five years matches his age and production level without overcommitting to a full star-length deal.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash (LW, 20, $1.20M) on five to six years.
recommendations.rationale: At 20 he is still developing and cheap. Lock him long before he prices himself up. The December note flagged him as a staggered core lock.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Tellqvist (G, 25, POTE high 90s, $0.80M) on four to five years.
recommendations.rationale: GM standing order: give him time to develop. Four to five years covers his development window and bridges the gap if Belfour walks.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Abid (LW, 24, 63 pts/49 GP, base TOUG 80 CHKG 80, $0.40M) on three to four years.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only internal toughness fix (standing order), the Coach needs him dressed, and at $400K he is the cheapest renewal on the roster. Do not trade him at the deadline.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Colaiacovo (D, 22, $1.10M) on three years, contingent on a real ice-time run this season.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach wants consecutive games for him at 18 MPG. Three years gives him a development window without a star-length commitment. Evaluate in February before offering.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Upshall (RW, 21, $1.20M) on two to three years.
recommendations.rationale: Evaluation deal for a 21-year-old on an expiring contract. Short term preserves flexibility.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Chistov (LW, 21, $1.10M) on two to three years.
recommendations.rationale: Evaluation deal. Was part of a Luongo package; with that dead he stays and gets a short renewal.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Alexeev (RW, 23, $1.10M) on two to three years.
recommendations.rationale: 23, expiring, depth forward. Short deal keeps the option to move him next summer if he does not develop.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Smirnov (LW, 20, $0.40M) on two to three years.
recommendations.rationale: 20, cheap, depth. Two to three years is the right evaluation length.

recommendations.summary: Keep Mogilny; reduce his role and plan his replacement next season rather than trying to trade him.
recommendations.rationale: He is not expiring, his declining production (0.87 from 1.62) and age (35) make him untradeable without a pick we do not own, and the remaining contract runs past this season. Ride him out.

recommendations.summary: Do not pursue Luongo this deadline. Florida demands a first-round pick and we do not own one.
recommendations.rationale: The Luongo target is confirmed as blocked by tor-no-picks-beyond-4th. Svehla and Roberts may recover a pick by the deadline, but that pick will be later than Florida demands. Revisit after June.

recommendations.summary: Open the Bell conversation in late February; CHI at 42 points are confirmed sellers and he closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously.
recommendations.rationale: 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE at age 24, $900K with 2 years left. The only player who addresses all three structural gaps on a re-signable contract from a losing club.

recommendations.summary: Add Avery to the LA target list alongside Belanger; he solves toughness, checking, and faceoffs at $400K with 2 years left.
recommendations.rationale: 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, age 25, $400K, 2 years, 51 GP 5 pts. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are sellers. Production is minimal but the role fit is exact.

recommendations.summary: Probe BOS on Thornton in late February; if they engage he solves scoring, toughness, checking, and faceoffs in one move, but their playoff position makes acceptance uncertain.
recommendations.rationale: 94 base, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 79 FACE, 73 pts in 47 GP, 25, $4.00M expiring. The Jan 25 vs Jan 22 discrepancy is resolved: base 94 is correct. BOS at 21-20-4 with 13 expiring deals could go either way.

recommendations.summary: If Thornton or Bell fall through, Conroy is the fallback centre: 63 points and 94 FACE at $2M from the worst team in the league.
recommendations.rationale: 85 base, 94 FACE, 63 pts in 51 GP, $2.00M expiring. CGY at 40 points with 10 expiring deals have no reason to keep him. Does not close toughness but fills the scoring-at-centre hole.

recommendations.summary: Chara remains the highest-toughness player available on a seller; any package must be restructured without Colaiacovo per the GM's Jan 19 veto.
recommendations.rationale: 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 85 base, 51 pts in 51 GP, 27, $1.70M expiring from OTT at 49 points with 11 expiring deals. The previous Eminger + Colaiacovo + R2 structure was vetoed; Svehla plus a mid-rounder is the alternative.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Bouwmeester from FLA; 21 years old with POTE 95 from the league's most expiring-heavy club gives the best long-term D upside available.
recommendations.rationale: 81 base, 95 POTE, 21, $1.20M expiring, 51 GP 19 pts. FLA at 44 points with 19 expiring contracts (league-high) are the most motivated sellers. He fills the future top-pair D slot alongside Eminger.

recommendations.summary: Komisarek remains the production-first option at young D; 59 points in 52 games at age 22 from MTL at 42 points.
recommendations.rationale: 77 base, 91 POTE, 22, $1.10M expiring, 52 GP 59 pts. MTL have 14 expiring deals. Replaces McCabe's declining 0.52 pts/g with a 22-year-old who produces like a first-pair D.

recommendations.summary: Savard folds into any ATL negotiation as a faceoff add-on; 88 FACE plus 55 points at $1M from a confirmed seller.
recommendations.rationale: 79 base, 88 FACE, 55 pts in 50 GP, 27, $1.00M expiring. ATL at 48 points with 11 expiring deals. Cheaper than Conroy and comes with the Kovalchuk/Heatley conversation.

recommendations.summary: Belanger is the cheapest pure faceoff fix; 97 FACE at $700K expiring from LA.
recommendations.rationale: 82 base, 97 FACE, $700K expiring, 51 GP 10 pts. Does not close toughness (no data suggests high TOUG) but solves the faceoff deficit at minimal cost. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring are sellers.

recommendations.proposed: Craig Conroy (CGY, C, 85 base, 94 FACE, 63 pts/51 GP, $2.00M, expiring, 31)
recommendations.summary: Open CGY conversation in late February: Chistov plus a 4th for Conroy's remaining season as a pure playoff rental with zero long-term commitment.
recommendations.rationale: Conroy's 94 FACE and 63 points at 85 base fill the centre-scoring and draw gap for the entire playoff run. Chistov is expiring anyway; we lose him for nothing in July unless we re-sign. CGY at 40 points with 10 expiring deals are the worst team and must liquidate; a 21-year-old with POTE 95 and 89 speed plus a pick is a rebuild asset. Payroll effect: +$900K for the rest of the season only, both deals expire in summer.

recommendations.current: Colaiacovo ($1.10M, expiring, 22, POTE 99) + Safronov ($0.90M, 23, 3 GP, unused)
recommendations.proposed: Mark Bell (CHI, LW, 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24, $900K, 2 years, 19 pts/51 GP)
recommendations.summary: Open CHI conversation in late February: Colaiacovo plus Safronov for Bell, who closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs permanently on a re-signable two-year deal at $900K.
recommendations.rationale: Bell is the only available player whose base grades close all three structural gaps simultaneously. CHI at 42 points are sellers and Bell's 19 points in 51 games make him depth, not a core piece. They get a 22-year-old with POTE 99 who projects top-pair and a 23-year-old with POTE 91 for D depth. We save $1.10M in salary. Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 fills Colaiacovo's slot. Acceptance is uncertain because CHI must value two unproven prospects over a known quantity.

recommendations.proposed: A 2nd or 3rd round draft pick from any contender needing veteran D depth
recommendations.summary: Move Svehla to a contender for a mid-round pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic; execute this regardless of whether Bell or Conroy approaches land.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla is 36, $3.60M, expiring, and over-80. Every contender needing a veteran blueliner for a playoff run is a buyer for half a season at $3.60M. This saves $3.60M immediately and creates the draft asset needed to sweeten the Bell package or fund a February acquisition. We do not intend to re-sign him. The pick-recovery mechanic works without knowing why; it is the only path to a pick better than a fourth-rounder this club has.

recommendations.proposed: Dress Tucker every night as a free bottom-six checking forward
recommendations.summary: If no trade closes the toughness gap, dress Tucker nightly for his 92 CHKG and 88 TOUG at no additional cost; he is already on the roster and has played 3 games.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker's 92 CHKG and 88 TOUG are the second-highest checking and toughness on the roster behind Roberts. At 29 with 2 years left at $1.30M he is on the books regardless. The coach has him dressed 3 times in 51 games. A tough physical series requires bodies; Tucker is the only unused one who brings those grades. This is a floor, not a ceiling.

recommendations.summary: Play Stahle in a stretch of games before the deadline; one appearance in 51 with POTE 96 is a wasted season.
recommendations.rationale: Age 20, POTE 96, 1 GP at 13 MPG. Every other young D on the club has 27+ games. He is dressed but never goes over the boards.

recommendations.summary: Spezza needs 12+ MPG consistently or his development window is closing; at 7.5 MPG and 0.41 pts/g his rate is falling not climbing.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, age 21, 15 points in 37 games on 7.5 MPG. January note set the threshold at 12 MPG and 0.60+ rate; he is below both. Scratching him now compounds the problem.

recommendations.summary: Give Colaiacovo a run of consecutive games; 53% share at 18 MPG is too sporadic for a 22-year-old building into a top-pair role.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99, 27 GP at 18 MPG (0.44 pts/g). The minutes per game are right. The problem is he sits every other night rather than building chemistry and consistency.

recommendations.summary: Upshall's rate has fallen to 0.38 pts/g; no promotion is warranted despite POTE 99.
recommendations.rationale: 17 points in 45 games on 10.7 MPG. Rate has declined from 0.40 at 43 GP. He is not earning more than fourth-line minutes.

recommendations.summary: Smirnov at POTE 70 and zero games is fine; his potential does not justify displacing anyone currently dressing.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 70 at age 20. Every other forward with 30+ games has higher potential and production. Being healthy is the right status for him.

recommendations.summary: Get Spezza to 12+ MPG or accept his development window is closing at 21.
recommendations.rationale: 5.3 MPG and rate fell to 0.38. I set a 12+ threshold on January 5th; he got half the minutes needed and the rate followed the minutes down. Either he plays or we stop counting on him.

recommendations.summary: Flag to GM: Fischer at 24 is declining (0.63 to 0.41) when he should be climbing, and his contract runs four more years.
recommendations.rationale: His rate dropped 35% in the recent window despite playing more (21.7 MPG). At 24, the expected direction is up. Not a trade recommendation, but the GM should know the trend before committing to him as the long-term second-pair defenceman.

recommendations.summary: McCabe's slump never ended: 0.52 pts/g in 27 recent games. The January 26th 'recovered' note was about his cumulative season rate, not current form.
recommendations.rationale: The 0.96 cumulative is propped up by a hot October. The last 27 games (since Dec 1) show 0.52 on 21.1 MPG. If this holds through February the top pair needs a solution.

recommendations.summary: Mogilny at 35 halved from 1.62 to 0.87 on 19.1 MPG. Plan for a reduced role or replacement next season.
recommendations.rationale: 35 years old, 19 minutes a night, producing half what he did in October. The decline is steep and the age makes a rebound unlikely.

recommendations.summary: Sundin at 33 dropped to 0.93 on 20 MPG. He is taking on more ice for less production; watch for overloading in February.
recommendations.rationale: 1.46 to 0.93 while minutes rose 16.9 to 20.0. That is the shape of a player being asked to carry more than his legs give. 31 games remain.

recommendations.summary: Stahle got one game at 13 MPG. Still far short of what a 20-year-old with his profile needs before the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: One dressing, zero points. My January 25th note said he needed at least one; he needs five or six to say anything about his readiness.

recommendations.summary: Leave Chlup where he is. Both his rate and minutes are climbing; the development is happening naturally.
recommendations.rationale: 0.62 to 0.67 pts/g, 11.0 to 15.8 MPG at 18. No intervention needed; the minutes are coming to him.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spezza against ATL and give him 12+ minutes to pull him out of the 86 morale hole.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza is at 7.5 MPG with 15 points in 37 games; his calibre puts him in the 17 MPG band and his morale is the lowest on the roster at 86, costing 1 point on every grade. ATL is 17-25 and this is a night where we can afford the development minutes.

recommendations.summary: No unit composition changes needed; the lines fit their jobs.
recommendations.rationale: L1 is elite in every category (checking 78 mean, faceoffs 88, scoring 86). L3 has the checking and speed to be a real third unit (71/91 checking, Chistov 95 speed). PK has three of our four 80+ checkers distributed across both kills. The units are coherent.

recommendations.summary: Keep L2's minutes moderate; do not expose them to ATL's top centre on draws.
recommendations.rationale: L2 faceoff mean is 56 (best is Chlup at 75). They will lose draws against any decent centre. Skilled lines with soft centres work when given softer matchups, not when asked to win the puck at the dot.

recommendations.summary: Stahle is dressed on the third pair but had 0 games played as of January 25; he needs to actually play.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 96 at 20 as a defenceman with zero games in 49+ is the biggest development waste on the roster. Being listed in a lineup slot means nothing without shifts. If tonight's game is winnable (ATL at 17-25), give him a few shifts.

recommendations.summary: Start Luongo. 92 OVR, no fatigue icon, ATL's 2.90 goals per game doesn't warrant resting him.
recommendations.rationale: Luongo is 92 OVR with 94 morale. ATL scores 2.90 per game, a mediocre offense outside their two stars. No fatigue icon on Luongo tonight.

recommendations.summary: Give Stahle a full start tonight. Their third pair (71 and 73 OVR) is the softest assignment available.
recommendations.rationale: Stahle was at zero games played through January 25. ATL's Boileau (71) and Kaberle (73) are the easiest pairing on their roster. If he's been dressing without playing, tonight is the night to commit.

recommendations.summary: No lineup changes. ATL is 17-25-2 with a 14.2% power play and Sutton out; every auto-pairing favors us. Normal development rotation applies.
recommendations.rationale: ATL's D is depleted (Sutton out until April), their PK is irrelevant, and their first line is dangerous but unmatched by design due to auto-pairing. We face their weakest first pair with our strongest line.

recommendations.summary: Move Salo at the deadline. $2.60M for two more years at 0.36 pts/g is dead weight.
recommendations.rationale: 8 points in 22 games, not dressed, and carries two years at $2.60M. No other D on the roster is worse value.

recommendations.summary: Trade Colaiacovo at the deadline. 0.44 pts/g on 18 MPG with an expiring deal is a sell.
recommendations.rationale: 12 points in 27 games, $1.10M expiring. He produces less than Eminger (0.48) and Klesla (0.45) while getting more minutes than Klesla.

recommendations.summary: Eminger is a trade candidate at the deadline unless he scores twice in the next four games; 0.48 pts/g is 0.03 above my cut.
recommendations.rationale: 19 points in 40 games. Season rate has slipped from 0.49 to 0.48 since January 26. Expiring at $1.20M. If he stays above 0.45, a late goal burst could make him a rental worth a pick.

recommendations.summary: Decide on Svehla before the deadline: extend him or trade him for assets. At 36 and $3.6M expiring, I lean trade.
recommendations.rationale: 0.68 pts/g in 34 games is solid but he will be 37 next year at that price. A pick or prospect now beats a decline later.

recommendations.summary: Stahle played his first game (1 GP). He needs to reach 15+ before season's end or we are wasting a high-potential defenceman.
recommendations.rationale: He went from 0 to 1 GP since January 25. Still the largest gap between potential and games on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Dress Abid (base TOUG 80, CHKG 80, 24) or Tucker (83 CHKG, 29) on the fourth line; neither is in any unit today.
recommendations.rationale: The roster has zero displayed toughness above 73. Abid's base is 80 and Tucker's checking is 83; both are on the roster and both are idle. Dressing one costs nothing and raises the floor.

recommendations.summary: Put Upshall (80 CHKG, 21) on the penalty kill; he is on the roster and in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: Checking depth is six players above 80 but two of them, Tucker and Upshall, are not lined. Upshall at 21 with 80 CHKG is the cheapest PK addition available.

recommendations.summary: Dress Koltsov (92 SPEE, 23) nightly; he is the third-fastest player on the club and in no unit.
recommendations.rationale: Koltsov produces at 1.09 ppg at 23 with 92 speed. The Coach flagged him in December and he remains unlined. This is the lowest-effort development gain on the roster.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, 24, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, $0.90M, 2y) is the only player in the league who closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously on a re-signable deal.
recommendations.rationale: No internal player has displayed FACE above 75 outside Sundin, and no player has displayed TOUG above 73. Bell solves both gaps at age 24. Open the conversation in late February per the GM's deadline timing order.

recommendations.summary: Luongo (FLA, 25, 91 base, POTE 96, $1.60M, 2y) remains the confirmed goalie target; FLA require Aebischer plus R1.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 39 and $6.50M is the best in net today but will not re-sign at that price. Luongo at 25 on a two-year deal is the permanent answer and the package is confirmed as Aebischer plus a first-round pick.

recommendations.summary: Scoring depth is adequate now: Gaborik 92, Afinogenov 90, Sundin 92, Mogilny 94 across four lines.
recommendations.rationale: Twelve players at 80+ overall provide scoring depth. The concern is the age curve above them, not their presence. No acquisition needed before the deadline for scoring.

recommendations.summary: Offer Gaborik a 5-6 year extension at $2.5-3.5M before July.
recommendations.rationale: 71 points in 50 games at 22, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring. His production makes him a market outlier; locking him at below-market through his mid-20s is the single biggest contract move available.

recommendations.summary: Offer Richards a 5-6 year extension at $2-3M before July.
recommendations.rationale: 51 points in 48 games at 24, $1.00M expiring. Same July market risk as Gaborik. Five years covers his prime and splits the re-negotiation from the depth group.

recommendations.summary: Offer Nash a 5-year extension before July.
recommendations.rationale: 30 points in 37 games at 20, POTE 95, $1.20M expiring. At his age and potential the next season's production could double his asking price. Five years at 25 protects through his best years.

recommendations.summary: Offer Eminger a 4-year extension, not 5-6, to stagger the renewal group.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, POTE 99, 19 points in 39 games, $1.20M expiring. Four years puts his next free agency in 2009, two summers later than Gaborik/Richards/Nash, splitting the payroll spike.

recommendations.summary: Offer Colaiacovo a 4-year extension alongside Eminger.
recommendations.rationale: Age 21, POTE 99, 12 points in 27 games, $1.10M expiring. Same staggering logic. Four years means the defence group and the forward group don't all renew at once.

recommendations.summary: Offer Kaberle a 3-year extension at $2.5-3M, not 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: Age 26, POTE 75 (ceiling set), 23 points in 42 games, $1.90M expiring. Three years covers him through 29, by which point Klesla (22, POTE 97, already 50 GP) holds the top-pair minutes.

recommendations.summary: No roster moves before late February; the deadline is 52 days away and the club is 14 points clear.
recommendations.rationale: TOR at 81 pts is not a seller. The deadline is 2005-03-19. Standing order says open negotiations late February, not now.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Luongo (FLA, 25, 91 base, POTE 96, $1.60M, 2yrs) for Aebischer plus own R1 before March 19.
recommendations.rationale: Solves the GM's January 15 goalie mandate, provides insurance if Belfour rejects a reduced renewal, and keeps a 25-year-old with two years already on his deal. Florida confirmed this is their price.

recommendations.summary: Add Savard (ATL, 27, 89 FACE, $1.00M expiring) at the deadline for the faceoff gap the Coach flagged.
recommendations.rationale: L4 faceoff mean is 52 with a best of 54. Savard at 89 FACE is the cheapest fix and ATL at 13-24-2 are motivated sellers.

recommendations.summary: If the Coach will dress Abid, the toughness gap closes internally at zero cost; if not, trade him before he walks.
recommendations.rationale: Abid carries 80 TOUG, 80 CHKG at $400K and the Coach has him in no unit. Either he plays or he becomes an above-80 asset moved for a pick.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik on 5-6 years at his next renewal window; do not let him reach free agency at 23 with POTE 90.
recommendations.rationale: 91 base, 67 points in 45 games, $1.10M. The cheapest elite winger on the market is about to double in price if he walks.

recommendations.summary: Renew Kaberle (26, $1.90M) on 5-6 years as the top-pairing blueliner.
recommendations.rationale: At 26 he is entering his prime. Losing him would force Eminger (21) into a role not yet earned.

recommendations.summary: Commit Eminger (21, POTE 99, $1.20M) on 5-6 years; the GM already vetoed trading him.
recommendations.rationale: POTE 99 at 21 is the highest ceiling on the blueline. His value only rises if he plays 20 MPG.

recommendations.summary: Renew Richards (24, $1.00M) on 5-6 years per the staggered-core plan.
recommendations.rationale: At 24 with a $1.00M expiring deal he is underpriced for what he provides. Locking him now prevents a July bidding war.

recommendations.summary: Renew Nash (20, $1.20M) on 5-6 years.
recommendations.rationale: A 20-year-old on $1.20M expiring is a club option waiting to be exercised. Lock him before his price rises.

recommendations.summary: Offer Belfour (39, $6.50M) two years at a reduced figure at renewal; expect rejection and plan for Luongo or Tellqvist as the successor.
recommendations.rationale: GM standing order says he stays as number one but the $6.50M at 39 is unsustainable. Two years at a lower number is the ask; if he walks the club must be ready.

recommendations.summary: Let Svehla (36, $3.60M) walk or move him at the deadline for a late pick; do not renew.
recommendations.rationale: At 36 with $3.60M expiring and Kaberle, Eminger and Colaiacovo behind him, he is the most obvious salary to shed. If above 80 base, the pick mechanic applies.

recommendations.summary: Do not renew Roberts (38, $2.70M); let him walk or move at the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach reports he is declining into February at 20 MPG. At 38 and $2.70M he is a rental already.

recommendations.summary: Shop Alexeev (23, 0.48 pts/g, 6.5 MPG, $1.10M expiring) at the deadline while he still carries trade value; do not re-sign.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged him as regressing from 0.62 to 0.48 pts/g with no role. His value is higher in February with a season of decent production on the sheet than in July with nothing.

recommendations.summary: Renew Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) on 2-3 years at flat salary; GM's standing order is to give him time.
recommendations.rationale: POTE in the high 90s per GM, costs nothing, and is the succession plan if Belfour walks. Two to three years keeps optionality without a star deal.

recommendations.summary: Sign Upshall (21), Chistov (21), Colaiacovo (21) and Smirnov (20) on 2-3 year deals; extend only those who earn it.
recommendations.rationale: All four are on $0.40M-$1.20M expiring deals at age 20-21. Two-year locks prevent the July scramble without over-committing to players whose ceilings are not yet proven.

recommendations.proposed: Samsonov (BOS, LW, 26, 89 base, 80 pts/45 GP, $1.90M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Trade Koltsov plus Tucker plus 4th-rounder to Boston for Samsonov; opens late February when BOS confirm they will not re-sign.
recommendations.rationale: BOS at 19-20-4 with 13 expiring deals and $26.05M profit are sorting their future. Koltsov at 23 with POTE 94 and 1.09 ppg is exactly the age profile they need; Tucker at 29 adds veteran checking depth for their young core. Toronto adds an 89-base 80-point LW for $0.50M less than they give. Acceptance uncertain but the hockey logic is clean for both sides.

recommendations.proposed: Belanger (LA, C, 27, 82 base, 91 FACE, 9 pts/48 GP, $0.70M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Trade Safronov to Los Angeles for Belanger; the cheapest faceoff fix available at $0.70M and 91 FACE.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 14-22-6 with 13 expiring deals are rebuilding. Safronov is 23 with POTE 91, CHKG 81, and three years of control at $0.90M; that is a cheap young blueliner for a rebuilding D corps. Belanger is a rental even for LA since he is expiring. Toronto closes the Coach's L4 faceoff gap (mean 52, best 54) for net $0.20M payroll reduction. Acceptance uncertain: LA may not value a 3-GP prospect.

recommendations.proposed: Havlat (OTT, RW, 23, 87 base, 64 pts/49 GP, $0.90M expiring, POTE 84)
recommendations.summary: Trade Upshall plus Alexeev to Ottawa for Havlat; adds a young 87-base scorer who is still developable alongside Gaborik and Richards.
recommendations.rationale: OTT at 16-24-5 with 11 expiring deals and $26.87M profit want young assets. Upshall is 21 with POTE 99 and 87 CHKG; Alexeev is 23 with POTE 94 and 28 points. Both fit a rebuild timeline. Toronto saves $1.40M net and acquires a 23-year-old at 64 points on $0.90M. The GM vetoed a richer Chara+Havlat package in January; this is a smaller ask that OTT should find easier to accept. Acceptance uncertain.

recommendations.current: Svehla (D, 36, 80+ base, $3.60M expiring) OR Roberts (LW, 38, 80+ base, $2.70M expiring)
recommendations.proposed: Draft pick (any round, per over-80 rental mechanic)
recommendations.summary: If any of the three above packages fails, trade Svehla or Roberts for a draft pick using the over-80 expiring mechanic; recovers capital the Luongo deal spent.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla at $3.60M and Roberts at $2.70M are both expiring veterans above 80 who will not be re-signed. The guide confirms this mechanic works. Either one recovers a pick for the March or summer window and sheds salary the team does not want to carry. Check their displayed overalls when negotiations open; both are close to 80 and may need a game-day reading.

recommendations.current: Chlup (sliding from L2C or Spezza on wing)
recommendations.summary: Put Spezza on the third line permanently to take him from 7.5 to 12+ MPG before February.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza has POTE 99 at 21, is producing 0.41 pts/g in 37 games with his rate climbing, and has been at 7.5 MPG since the January 5th flag. He needs 12+ minutes to consolidate his development and nothing has changed in three weeks.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle for at least one game before the trade deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Stahle has POTE 96 at 20 as a defenceman and has not played a single game in 50. Four other young defencemen have games and none has a higher scouting number. Flagged January 25th and still unresolved.

recommendations.summary: Leave Upshall where he is; he is earning his minutes and a promotion is not justified.
recommendations.rationale: Upshall has POTE 99 but is at 0.38 pts/g on 10.7 MPG, which is fourth-line production. He is getting what his play has earned. A high scouting number does not buy ice time.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 12+ minutes or acknowledge the development experiment has failed; at 5.3 MPG and 0.38 pts/g he is losing not gaining.
recommendations.rationale: The January 5th note set a floor: 12+ MPG at 0.60+ or the window closes. He is now below both thresholds and trending down on each.

recommendations.proposed: Stahle in the lineup or on a recall
recommendations.summary: Stahle has played zero games at 20 with POTE 96. Dress him at least once before the trade deadline.
recommendations.rationale: Fifty games in and he has not suited up. A prospect with 96 potential at defenceman is wasting an entire season on the press box.

recommendations.summary: Flag to the GM that Abid at 1.39 pts/g since the first save is the team's best scorer and his contract situation should be addressed before this runs away.
recommendations.rationale: 1.09 to 1.39 pts/g between saves is the biggest improvement on the roster. If his contract expires this makes him the highest-leverage renewal on the team.

recommendations.summary: Leave Chlup exactly where he is; 0.69 pts/g on rising minutes at 18 is the best growth story on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Production up from 0.62 to 0.69 while minutes went 11.0 to 15.6. Do not disrupt this.

recommendations.summary: Eminger stays on the first pair; 0.69 pts/g on 17.4 MPG confirms the breakout across a five-week window.
recommendations.rationale: The January 1st note said it was real. Five more weeks at this rate makes it permanent.

recommendations.summary: Dress Spezza on a regular shift (L3 or L4) to lift him from 7.5 MPG toward the 10 MPG his calibre band expects; his morale at 86 is costing -1 to every grade.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza is 21, at 86 morale (trending -4), getting 7.5 MPG on a 10 MPG band. He has been at 86 for many saves, indicating sustained under-usage. Development and morale are the same problem: he needs game minutes.

recommendations.summary: No line changes warranted for morale beyond Spezza; the room averages 92 with only two players below 90.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin (93, -4) and Mogilny (89) are slightly under their minutes bands but at 33 and 35 respectively, moving them up breaks L1/L2 chemistry and risks fatigue. Alexeev (89, -4) is close to his band and has not yet crossed into the 80s penalty zone.

recommendations.summary: We have no faceoff winner above 80 except Sundin. L3 (58 mean) and L4 (53 mean) lose draws and start deep in our zone.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin 91, Chlup 78, Richards 75, then 55s. Against centre-heavy teams we cannot win the draw on two of four lines. No rearrangement fixes this; we need a player above 80 in the discipline.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle at least once before the deadline on a night we can afford it.
recommendations.rationale: 20 years old, POTE 96, 0 games in 49. He is the biggest development waste on the roster.

recommendations.summary: All eight units are correctly constructed for their roles. No composition change recommended.
recommendations.rationale: L1 balances offense and checking. L2 is built to score (92/92 on Mogilny and Afinogenov) and is soft by design. L3 has the best checker (Richards 94) and best stamina (86) on the roster. L4's stamina ceiling (60 mean) is structural, not fixable by personnel within this roster.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour; Luongo carries the tired-goalie icon today.
recommendations.rationale: Standing order from Jan 19: a tired goalie does not start. Luongo's streak cell reads 'a tired goaltender'; Belfour's is clear at 93 OVR. On the road, we need a fresh net.

recommendations.summary: No line changes for Carolina.
recommendations.rationale: Their top pair is Ozolinsh 82 / Dandenault 74; Gaborik's 99 speed already mismatches them. Their PP is 17.2% and their bottom six averages 69 OVR. No unit needs reshuffling to beat this opponent.

recommendations.summary: No defensive lineup changes for Carolina; all pairs healthy and performing.
recommendations.rationale: No defenceman injuries (q44). McCabe (48 pts/50 GP, 22.4 MPG), Svehla (23 pts/34 GP, 22.2 MPG), Kaberle (23 pts/42 GP on a flame icon), Fischer (22 pts/45 GP) are all fit and producing. The pairs are set.

recommendations.proposed: Abid (on roster, base TOUG 80, base CHKG 80, 24, not lined)
recommendations.summary: Line Abid nightly; he is the only rostered player with base toughness at 80 and the coach is not using him.
recommendations.rationale: Zero players display 80+ TOUG today. Abid's base TOUG is 80, his base CHKG is 80, and he is on the roster in no unit. Tucker at 70 base TOUG is the coach's current floor, which is 10 points lower. This is a free roster asset being wasted.

recommendations.current: nobody above 80 TOUG base except Abid at 80
recommendations.proposed: Bell (CHI, C, 24, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 80 base ovr, $900K, 2yrs)
recommendations.summary: Bell remains the toughness upgrade over Abid (95 TOUG vs 80, 93 CHKG vs 80) and is re-signable at 24 with two years left.
recommendations.rationale: Abid at 80/80 is the floor. Bell at 95/93/87 FACE in one player covers the two worst roles on the roster plus the faceoff gap. Proposed price: R2 plus Colaiacovo. CHI profitable at $26M so acceptance requires a real package. Open negotiations late February per GM's standing order.

recommendations.current: Sundin (90 FACE, 33) is the only 80+ option; Richards at 70 is the best backup
recommendations.proposed: Savard (ATL, C, 27, 89 FACE, 48 pts/43 GP, $1M expiring)
recommendations.summary: Savard at 89 FACE is the cheapest faceoff solution and folds into the ATL Kovalchuk conversation at no extra pick cost.
recommendations.rationale: One 80+ faceoff man at age 33 is not a plan for next season. Savard at 89 FACE, 27, $1M expiring from ATL (13-24-2, 11 expiring deals) is the target. He is a centre, which resolves the wing-position objection the GM raised against Bell for this slot on Jan 25.

recommendations.summary: Spezza's 5.3 MPG is a roster-construction problem with no internal fix; accept the stall this year and revisit in summer when a trade or departure opens a top-nine slot.
recommendations.rationale: The coach is right that no unlined depth (Salo 88, Koltsov 92 speed, Tucker 83 CHKG) can be swapped for ice without weakening the lineup. At 35-8-3 the club is contending and cannot sacrifice a top-nine regular for a prospect. This is a 2005-06 planning item.

recommendations.current: Roberts (38) covers CHKG 86, HERO 90, INJU 98 simultaneously
recommendations.summary: No other player holds two of Roberts' three 80+ roles; his departure is a 2006 multi-role gap and argues for acquiring keepable young toughness now, not rentals.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla at 36 carries CHKG 83 and HERO 90 but is one year younger than McCabe. McCabe carries CHKG 86 and INJU 94 but is 29. The 20-year-olds with 80+ in any of those roles: none listed in the top-6 for checking, clutch, or durability.

recommendations.summary: Lock Gaborik on 5-6 years before July; at 22 with 70 points in 49 games and POTE 90, he is the most valuable asset on the roster and the only one whose price will spike after a 70-point season.
recommendations.rationale: His current $1.10M is a fifth of what a 91-base 70-point winger will command in July. Five-year deals at $5-7M per year are the correct structure per the manual's star guidance.

recommendations.summary: Extend Chlup on 5-6 years now at his rookie price; at 18 with POTE 95 and 26 points in 38 games, a full top-nine season erases his current $2.34M contract value.
recommendations.rationale: He has two years left, so this is possible mid-term. The price differential between extending now at $2-3M versus re-signing after a 50-point sophomore year at $5-7M is real money across five years.

recommendations.summary: Sign Richards to 5-6 years at 24 with 51 points and POTE 88; he anchors the centre group alongside Sundin for the next five seasons.
recommendations.rationale: At $1.00M expiring, his price will jump. Five years at $3-5M keeps him under team control through age 29, which is his prime.

recommendations.proposed: Rebuild draft capital through veteran expiries
recommendations.summary: Svehla ($3.60M, 36, POTE 55) and Roberts ($2.70M, 38, POTE 52) should go for picks rather than walk for nothing in July; the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic applies to Roberts at 87 base.
recommendations.rationale: Toronto's draft capital appears almost spent (only a round-4 pick noted). Every R2-R4 acquired before the deadline is a chip for next summer's Luongo or ATL conversation. Roberts at 87 base with POTE 52 qualifies for the trade-for-pick mechanic.

recommendations.summary: The age curve is sound: 16 at 23 or under with six carrying POTE 95+, and the 24-29 group of ten bridges to the prime years without a gap.
recommendations.rationale: After this summer's veteran expiries, the roster shifts to Sundin (34), Mogilny (36), McCabe (30), and the young core — exactly the 5-7 veteran shape the manual prescribes. No structural intervention is needed on the age curve itself.

recommendations.summary: Execute the Luongo trade in late February: send Aebischer plus own R1 to Florida.
recommendations.rationale: Solves the goalie mandate from Jan 15. Luongo is 25, 91 base, POTE 96, $1.60M, two years left. Florida confirmed they only accept Aebischer plus R1 (not Chistov). Aebischer is expendable given Belfour stays and Tellqvist develops.

recommendations.summary: Pursue Komisarek in late February if MTL are selling; package a second-rounder plus a depth piece.
recommendations.rationale: MTL at 12-24-4 with 14 expiring deals are in full rebuild. Komisarek is 22 with POTE 91 at $1.10M expiring, producing like a first-pair D. If the R1 is spent on Luongo, build around a DET-2nd or similar.

recommendations.proposed: Trade for a draft pick if 80+ base
recommendations.summary: If Svehla reads above 80 base, move him before the deadline for a draft pick.
recommendations.rationale: At 36 and $3.60M we are not re-signing him. The above-80-for-a-pick mechanic converts him into a future asset. $3.60M in savings.

recommendations.proposed: Trade for a draft pick if 80+ base
recommendations.summary: If Roberts reads above 80 base, move him before the deadline for a draft pick.
recommendations.rationale: At 38 and $2.70M he is a pure rental. Same mechanic as Svehla. Combined with Svehla, $6.30M in summer savings.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Smirnov; move before the deadline for a late pick or release.
recommendations.rationale: Coach flagged him on Jan 25: zero games played, lowest POTE in the young group at 70. He is not earning a roster spot.

recommendations.proposed: Kaberle, Eminger, Nash, Gaborik, Richards on 5-6 years
recommendations.summary: Lock the five core young players on 5-6 year deals in July.
recommendations.rationale: All five expire this summer between $1.00M and $1.90M. Without long deals they hit free agency simultaneously in July and ratchet against each other. Eminger at POTE 99 and Gaborik at POTE 90, 67 pts/45 GP are the priorities.

recommendations.proposed: Upshall, Chistov, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Abid, Tellqvist on 2-3 years
recommendations.summary: Re-sign the six depth pieces on 2-3 year deals in July.
recommendations.rationale: They are useful but should not be locked long. Combined they are $5.80M; on 2-3 years they provide flexibility for the second wave of young players coming through the draft.

recommendations.summary: Keep Belfour through the playoffs; do not trade him. Plan for him to walk at renewal.
recommendations.rationale: GM standing order: he is the best goalie we have and we need a number one now. At 39 he will likely refuse a reduced rate and leave. Luongo fills the gap going forward.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Marleau from SJ to take over C1; he is 89 base with 78 points in 50 games at 25 on a $1.60M expiring deal from a 16-23-7 club with 14 expiring contracts.
recommendations.rationale: No available player matches his production-to-cost ratio. SJ are rebuilding and cannot re-sign him; his $1.60M is cheaper than any replacement we'd develop. He and Sundin are both elite playmakers who can coexist on the same roster.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Gagne from PHI at 86 base, 71 points in 47 games, 24, $2.40M expiring; PHI have $69.34M payroll with $7.74M profit and must shed salary.
recommendations.rationale: PHI are the most salary-burdened club in the league. Gagne at $2.40M on a bad team with 12 expiring deals is a natural dump. He fills the wing slot beside Marleau or Sundin without competing with our existing wingers for minutes.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Sulku from CGY at 75 base with POTE 92, TOUG 89, CHKG 87, 20, $0.94M expiring, as a toughness prospect who could become a regular in two seasons.
recommendations.rationale: He is the only player on a selling club who combines 85+ TOUG/CHKG with POTE above 90 at age 20. Only 5 points in 34 games means he cannot contribute immediately, but his physical profile is exactly what this roster lacks long-term. His $0.94M expiring deal makes him cheap to acquire.

recommendations.summary: Acquire Brad Stuart from SJ at 87 base, 38 points in 50 games, age 25, $1.80M, one year remaining; SJ are in full rebuild mode with 14 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla at 36 with POTE 55 is a one-year rental. Stuart at 25 with 87 base is the replacement who also fixes the 30-33 age gap on defence. He pairs with Eminger to form a young top-four.

recommendations.summary: ATL remain the primary deadline target: Kovalchuk at 89 base, 78 points in 41 games, 21, $1.10M expiring, or Heatley at 91 base, 74 points in 38 games, 23, same contract.
recommendations.rationale: Already tracked. ATL at 15-25-2 with 11 expiring and $20.57M profit are confirmed sellers. He uses our single remaining R1 plus Koltsov. This trade and the Luongo trade compete for that pick; one must take priority.

recommendations.summary: Luongo (FLA, 91 base, POTE 96, 25, $1.60M, 2 years) remains the GM's confirmed goalie mandate; price is R1 plus Chistov per GM confirmation.
recommendations.rationale: Already on the books. FLA at 17-25-4 are non-contenders. This deal and the ATL deal both require our single first-rounder; the GM must choose one.

recommendations.summary: Savard (ATL, 89 FACE, 27, $1.00M expiring) is the only faceoff solution available on a seller; fold him into the ATL conversation alongside Kovalchuk or Heatley.
recommendations.rationale: The league-wide search for 85+ FACE on clubs below 50 points returned nothing else. Savard is the sole option and costs no additional pick beyond what ATL already require.

recommendations.summary: Bell (CHI, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 80 base, 24, $0.90M, 2 years) remains the toughness upgrade that closes all three gaps simultaneously; proposed price R2 plus Colaiacovo.
recommendations.rationale: CHI at 13-26-7 are the worst team in the league with 10 expiring deals. They are profitable at $26.01M so acceptance requires a real package, but Bell's profile is unmatched on any seller. His 2 years of control separates him from rental-level toughness acquisitions.

recommendations.summary: Chara (OTT, 85 base, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 45 points in 41 games, 27, $1.70M expiring) adds toughness from the blueline; OTT at 16-24-5 are confirmed rebuild.
recommendations.rationale: Already tracked. He replaces Svehla (36, POTE 55, expiring) with a 27-year-old who produces 1.1 pts/g from the position. The GM vetoed the Eminger package but a different return structure may work.

recommendations.summary: Havlat (OTT, 87 base, 61 points in 42 games, 23, $0.90M expiring) pairs with Chara in the same negotiation to add scoring without a second pick.
recommendations.rationale: Already tracked. Two OTT targets in one conversation reduces negotiation cost. He is 23 with scoring upside and fits our age curve perfectly.

recommendations.summary: Trade Safronov to LA for Belanger to close the faceoff gap without spending our round-4 pick.
recommendations.rationale: LA at 13-20-5 lose Belanger for nothing in July unless they deal. Safronov gives them a POTE-91 D with three years of control for their rebuild. We save $200K and get a 90-FACE centre for the playoff run.

recommendations.summary: Trade Chistov plus the R4 to ATL for Savard if LA decline Belanger.
recommendations.rationale: ATL at 13-24-2 with 11 expiring deals lose Savard for nothing otherwise. Chistov at POTE 95 with 89 speed gives them a high-ceiling winger plus a pick. Costs our last draft asset and a POTE-95 forward for an expiring centre.

recommendations.summary: Trade Colaiacovo to CHI for Bell as the premium keeper option if both faceoff trades die.
recommendations.rationale: Bell closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously at age 24 on two years. Colaiacovo is surplus behind Eminger (POTE 99) and Klesla (POTE 97). CHI at $26M profit are not desperate; a POTE-99 blueliner may exceed their valuation of Bell. Acceptance uncertain.

recommendations.summary: Dress Abid every night on the bottom six; his base 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG are the only rostered 80+ in either category.
recommendations.rationale: No other rostered player displays 80+ in toughness today; Abid clears it at 80 base and carries 63 points in 49 games at $400K. The coach's report never mentions him.

recommendations.summary: Release Smirnov: age 20, POTE 70, zero games this season, $400K, lowest potential in the young group.
recommendations.rationale: The coach flagged him as not earning a roster spot. He occupies a slot and contributes nothing.

recommendations.summary: Dress Stahle for at least one of the next three games. POTE 96 at 20 with zero games in 49 is the biggest development waste on the roster.
recommendations.rationale: Colaiacovo and Safronov both get rotation minutes; Stahle has higher potential than Safronov (96 vs 91) and hasn't played once. Colaiacovo's 27 games came from the same rotation slot Stahle should be sharing.

recommendations.summary: Spezza needs 12+ MPG. At 7.5 and POTE 99 he is wasting the ceiling and morale is showing it (86).
recommendations.rationale: Season rate of 0.41 pts/g on 7.5 MPG means he hasn't had a chance to show what his ceiling holds. Morale at 86 puts him in the -1 penalty band. He needs a real shift allocation for 10+ games before anyone can judge him.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev's 0.55 pts/g on 8.8 MPG says he deserves 12+ minutes. He's been the most efficient young forward all season and the most underused.
recommendations.rationale: 27 points in 49 games on the lowest ice allocation of any regular. At 23 with POTE 94 he is producing at a rate that warrants a top-nine role, not fourth-line scraps.

recommendations.summary: The top four young players are all earning their minutes. No action needed.
recommendations.rationale: Nash 0.83 pts/g on 12.9 MPG, Gaborik 1.43 on 19.1, Klesla 0.47 on 15.3 at 49 games, Eminger 0.49 season with a 0.79 recent rate on 16.0 MPG. Each is producing at or above his ice allocation.

recommendations.proposed: Spezza at 12+ MPG on wing if centre is taken
recommendations.summary: Give Spezza at least 12 minutes a night as a winger if the fourth-line centre is locked, or accept he is not a future second-line centre.
recommendations.rationale: Spezza at 21 has 0.38 pts/g on 5.3 MPG across 37 games. His rate dropped from 0.43 while his ice halved from 9.1. This is the third recommendation; the development window at 21 is closing. If the GM will not give him 12+, his value shifts from future piece to trade chip.

recommendations.summary: Alexeev at 23 is regressing (0.62 to 0.48 pts/g, 11.1 to 6.5 MPG) and has no role; flag him as a trade candidate while he still carries value.
recommendations.rationale: A 23-year-old declining on both production and minutes is unusual and suggests the developmental bet has failed. At 0.48 on 6.5 MPG he is worse than our fourth-liners and still young enough to interest another club.

recommendations.summary: Flag to GM: Sundin, Mogilny and Roberts are all declining into February at 20 MPG each; the L3 stamina ceiling forces this, and the plan should assume they have less left in the tank than their season totals suggest.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin 1.46 to 0.84 on 16.9 to 19.9 MPG at 33. Mogilny 1.62 to 0.90 on 16.9 to 18.6 at 35. Roberts 1.29 to 1.04 on 16.5 to 20.0 at 38. All three are absorbing more ice because young lines cannot handle it, and all three are producing less. February will be harder than the records show.

recommendations.summary: Chlup at 18 is producing 0.72 on 15.2 MPG and climbing; let the line keep building without disrupting it for now.
recommendations.rationale: His rate rose from 0.62 while minutes went from 11.0 to 15.2. That is real development happening in game. No intervention needed.

recommendations.summary: Give Spezza 12+ minutes on a higher line at the next opportunity to lift him from 86 morale toward 90+.
recommendations.rationale: He's at 7.5 mpg and 86 morale, below his expected band regardless of whether his calibre is 70-79 (band 10) or 80-89 (band 17). At 0.41 pts/g he's producing on the ice he gets; the only lever is more of it. The GM's rotation philosophy justifies scratching him on development nights, but 86 has been stable for weeks without recovery, so the next non-maximize game should put him back in.

recommendations.summary: No other player needs a minutes adjustment for morale tonight.
recommendations.rationale: Chlup at 86 is on 13.8 mpg above his likely 10-minute band; Luongo at 87 is trending up after his dip; everyone else is at 89+ and stable. The room is healthy.

recommendations.summary: We need a faceoff-capable fourth-line centre at the deadline; nobody on L4 can win a draw (faceoff mean 52, best 54) and all four available faceoff men above 74 are committed elsewhere.
